subtopic: Loop reordering / GEMM ikj vs. ijk
learningObjective: Compare two loop orderings of a naive GEMM for their locality behavior and identify which is legal and preferred on a row-major layout.
stem: Two loop orderings of naive GEMM are shown. All matrices are row-major FP32. Compared to Order 1 (ijk), which correctly describes Order 2 (ikj)?

options.text: Order 2 is not semantically equivalent to Order 1 because it accumulates into `C[i,j]` in a different order; floating-point non-associativity makes the two answer matrices different.
Order 2 is semantically equivalent but has worse locality: unit-stride writes to `C` cost more than unit-stride reads from `B`, so Order 1 remains preferred on row-major.
Order 2 is illegal because it introduces a loop-carried dependence on `C[i,j]` that did not exist in Order 1; the reordering violates SSA form.

Order 2 is semantically equivalent (same +='s over the same triples) and has better spatial locality on row-major storage: the innermost loop reads `B[k,:]` and writes `C[i,:]` with unit stride, unlike Order 1 which strides through `B` by N.

explanation: Both orders compute the same set of multiply-accumulates on the same triples (i,j,k); the reduction on `C[i,j]` is +='s over `k`, so any permutation over `(j,k)` is semantically equivalent modulo FP non-associativity (typically ignored for GEMM correctness testing). Order 2 (ikj) is preferred on row-major layouts: the innermost `j` loop walks `B[k, 0..N]` and `C[i, 0..N]` with unit stride (cache-friendly, vectorizable), while Order 1's innermost `k` loop walks `B[0..K, j]` with stride `N` (cache-unfriendly). Option A over-states FP non-associativity as a correctness issue; option C is wrong (the dependence is a reduction on `C[i,j]`, present in both orders); option D reverses the locality direction.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: while FP addition is non-associative, GEMM reductions are treated as commutative/associative in practice; the two orders are considered semantically equivalent for optimization.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the reduction dependence exists in both orders; SSA is preserved by both.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: standard textbook explanation of the ikj vs. ijk locality difference on row-major.

assumptions: Row-major storage for all three matrices.
FP non-associativity is treated as a numerical concern, not a correctness concern for GEMM.
nonImplications: Does not imply ikj is optimal — blocked / vectorized orderings dominate in practice.
Does not imply the same order is preferred on column-major layouts (Fortran / BLAS-style would prefer jki).

distractorRationales.A: Overstates FP-non-associativity impact on optimization equivalence.
distractorRationales.C: Confuses reduction dependence with SSA violation.

performanceClaim.scope: Row-major naive GEMM cache behavior across loop orderings
